ambiguities_or_notes: The page marker, title, fable label, and complete narrative are represented; the exact source SHA-256 matched the mounted audited Russian snapshot.
«велики и развилисты» is rendered 'large and branching', keeping the visible shape of the antlers rather than substituting a more decorative adjective.
«ноги мои плохи и жидки» is kept conservatively as 'my legs are bad and thin'. The source's simple evaluative contrast matters to the fable and is not polished into 'frail' or another abstraction.
«Он уходил» is 'He was getting away', preserving the sense that the legs were in fact saving him before the forest reverses his advantage.

The closing contrast keeps Tolstoy's repeated concrete reference to the body parts: 'The ones I thought were bad and thin were saving me, and the ones I admired are what ruined me.' Reverse target-to-source audit found no substantive omission or unsupported addition.
